With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale. Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort. Summary/Objective The Critical Operations Technician provides 24×7×365 operational coverage to support continuous, safe and reliable performance of critical electrical, mechanical, cooling, controls and life-safety systems across the data centre. The role performs hands-on operational maintenance, system monitoring, first-response troubleshooting, incident support and contractor coordination to uphold STACK’s 100% uptime commitment. Technicians operate and monitor facility infrastructure across power and cooling paths within approved procedures and role-specific authorisations, while maintaining a concierge-level customer service approach in all stakeholder interactions. Essential Functions – Critical Operations Maintain 24×7×365 shift coverage, ensuring safe and stable operation of all critical infrastructure systems. Operate and monitor critical electrical and/or mechanical systems (based on background, training and authorisation) including UPS, PDUs, switchboards, generators, CDU/FWU/CRAC/CRAH units, chilled water systems, pumps and associated plant—strictly within approved operating procedures. Perform hands-on operational maintenance within authorised scope, including inspections, condition monitoring, equipment resets, minor adjustments and component-level replacements (non-licenced work). Identify abnormal conditions, complete initial diagnostics, implement first-level rectification actions where authorised, and escalate promptly to the Senior Data Centre Specialist. Respond to alarms and operational incidents, supporting containment, investigation, communication and restoration activities. Use BMS/EPMS and monitoring platforms to track alarms, interpret trends and support performance optimisation within approved limits. Complete structured rounds including meter readings, thermal/capacity checks and condition observations, recording findings accurately. Coordinate and supervise licenced contractors performing trade-restricted works, ensuring compliance with permits, LOTO and site safety requirements. Support planned maintenance, shutdowns, testing and return-to-service activities through operational tasks, witnessing and verification. Maintain accurate shift logs, event records, handover notes and CMMS updates to ensure full operational traceability. Proactively identify and report reliability risks and improvement opportunities to support STACK’s 100% uptime commitment. Participate in incident management training and exercises, acting as a trained first responder under direction of incident leaders. Contribute to continuous improvement of SOPs, MOPs, EOPs, risk assessments and operational readiness activities. Provide professional, timely communication to customers and stakeholders to support a high-quality service experience. This role does not perform licenced electrical, mechanical or refrigeration work. All trade-restricted activities are undertaken by appropriately qualified contractors or licenced personnel. The role focuses on operational system management, first-response troubleshooting, vendor coordination and component-level maintenance within authorised limits. People Set a high standard for safety behaviour, operational discipline and professional conduct across the shift. Support technicians through on-the-job coaching, demonstrations and constructive feedback to improve capability and consistency. Assist with onboarding and familiarisation of new team members, reinforcing authorised boundaries and operational expectations. Strengthen team communication by ensuring clear handovers, accurate escalation details and calm coordination during events. Participate actively in briefings, toolbox talks, training and operational discussions, offering practical observations and improvement ideas. Build collaborative relationships with Security, Projects and vendor personnel to support safe, coordinated site operations. Demonstrate a concierge‑level customer service approach in all interactions with customers, visitors and stakeholders. Competencies Operational discipline with a strong focus on safety, risk control and reliability Ability to operate critical electrical and/or mechanical systems within procedural and authorisation boundaries Effective troubleshooting, root-cause thinking and first-response decision-making under pressure Ability to interpret alarms, trends and technical documentation (SLDs, O&M manuals, procedures) Proficient in digital operational systems (BMS/EPMS, CMMS, workflow platforms) and reporting tools Strong communication skills and calm, structured incident support Contractor coordination capability with sound permit-to-work and LOTO awareness Customer-focused, professional service orientation Collaborative team behaviour with personal accountability and consistency on shift Continuous improvement approach (procedures, logs, risk reduction and operational uplift) Preferred Education And Experience 2-3 years' experience in critical environments such as data centres, hospitals, utilities, defence, industrial plants or similar operational settings. Demonstrated capability operating and/or monitoring electrical and/or mechanical infrastructure (e.g., UPS, generators, switchgear, PDUs/PMMs, ATS/STS, CRAC/CRAH, chilled water systems, pumps, fire systems and controls). Hands-on experience performing operational maintenance and first-level rectification activities within authorised limits. Experience using BMS/EPMS and CMMS/workflow tools to manage alarms, work orders and operational documentation. Ability to interpret technical drawings and documentation (including single-line diagrams and O&M manuals). Familiarity with permit-to-work, LOTO and basic risk assessment principles. Strong written and verbal communication skills suitable for shift logs, incident updates and customer/stakeholder engagement. Work Environment/Conditions Role operates on a 24×7 rotating shift roster including nights, weekends and public holidays. Work occurs in data halls, plant rooms, electrical/mechanical spaces and external plant areas; PPE is required as per site policy. Participation in emergency response activities and incident exercises is required. Work Authorization/Security Clearance Requirements Legal entitlement to work in Australia. Ability to satisfy pre-employment screening requirements (as applicable), including right-to-work checks, background checks and reference checks. Ability to meet data centre security requirements including badging, access control and adherence to customer-mandated security protocols. Security clearance is not required unless specified for a customer-specific facility. Equal Opportunity Employer STACK provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. review_candidates.title: Conference Producer - Global MedTech & HealthTech
review_candidates.description: About MedTech World Launched in 2020, MedTech World began with a mission to position Malta as a meeting point for the global MedTech and HealthTech ecosystem. Today, we've grown into an international platform operating across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Asia, bringing together founders, investors, healthcare systems, clinicians, corporates, policymakers and industry leaders. Our global calendar spans flagship summits in Malta, Dubai, West Palm Beach and Hong Kong, alongside investor forums, executive gatherings, roadshows, workshops and curated networking experiences throughout the year. As we continue to expand internationally, we're looking for an ambitious and highly organised Conference Producer to take ownership of the content and programming behind our global events. This isn't simply about filling an agenda. The Role You'll be responsible for identifying the conversations that matter, finding the right people to lead them, and turning those ideas into compelling panels, keynotes, fireside chats and experiences. Working closely with our CEO and wider leadership team, you'll have direct exposure to some of the most exciting companies, investors, healthcare leaders and innovators shaping the future of healthcare. Role Description/ What you'll Do. As Conference Producer, you'll take ownership of the programme from the earliest research stage through to execution on-site. Own the end-to-end conference programme across MedTech World's international events, from initial research and agenda development through speaker confirmation and on-site delivery. Research the latest developments across MedTech, HealthTech, digital health, AI, medical devices, biotechnology, healthcare systems and investment to identify the conversations our audiences need to hear. Develop compelling conference themes, tracks, panel discussions, fireside chats, keynotes and new content formats. Identify and recruit high-calibre speakers including CEOs, founders, investors, clinicians, hospital executives, corporate leaders, academics and policymakers. Lead speaker outreach, invitations and follow-ups, building genuine long-term relationships rather than treating speakers as one-off event participants. Carefully curate panels, ensuring the right balance of expertise, geography, perspectives and personalities on stage. Help with writing strong session titles, descriptions, speaker briefs, moderator notes and agenda copy. Prepare speakers and moderators ahead of each event so conversations are focused, engaging and valuable to the audience. Maintain accurate speaker pipelines, programme schedules, confirmations and deadlines across multiple international events simultaneously. Work closely with our partnerships team to integrate sponsored content while protecting the quality and credibility of the overall programme. Collaborate with our marketing and media teams to identify speakers, sessions and stories that can become interviews, articles, social content and wider campaigns. Work closely with operations and production teams to ensure the programme translates seamlessly from the agenda document to the stage. Be present on-site at our international summits, managing speakers, troubleshooting programme changes and helping ensure every session runs successfully. Where appropriate, moderate panels, conduct interviews or host conversations yourself. Analyse feedback and programme performance after each event and continuously improve our content strategy. Develop new ideas for Investor Forums, CEO gatherings, workshops, roundtables, retreats and other executive formats beyond the traditional conference stage. Build and maintain a strong international network of potential speakers and contributors across the healthcare innovation ecosystem. Location: Remote. Open to candidates across Europe, provided they are eligible to work in their country of residence. Relocation to our Malta HQ is also welcomed and supported. What We're Looking For? We're looking for someone who combines curiosity, commercial awareness, editorial judgement and exceptional organisation. You should be comfortable spending the morning researching an emerging healthcare technology, the afternoon speaking with a global CEO or investor, and still making sure dozens of speaker confirmations and programme deadlines are moving forward. Ideally, you'll bring: Previous experience in conference production, agenda development, content production, journalism, research or a similar role. A strong interest in healthcare, technology, entrepreneurship and investment. Excellent research skills and the ability to quickly understand unfamiliar or technically complex subjects. Strong editorial judgement — knowing the difference between a topic that sounds interesting and one that will actually create a great conversation on stage. Excellent written and spoken English. Confidence communicating with senior executives, investors, clinicians, government representatives and international stakeholders. Experience with speaker recruitment, outreach and relationship management. Exceptional organisation and attention to detail. The ability to manage large numbers of speakers, deadlines and moving pieces across several international events simultaneously. A proactive mentality — you don't wait to be told which speaker to contact or which topic to research next. The ability to work quickly and calmly when agendas inevitably change. Strong collaboration skills across production, marketing, partnerships, media and operations. Comfort working independently and as part of a distributed international team. Ability and willingness to travel internationally for MedTech World summits and other key events throughout the year. A background in Life Sciences, Medicine, Healthcare, Journalism, Communications, Business or Events is an advantage, but we're much more interested in your ability to research, think, communicate and execute. What Success Looks Like? Success in this role means building programmes that people genuinely want to attend. It means securing speakers who elevate the MedTech World brand, identifying important conversations before they become obvious, and creating panels with genuine chemistry rather than simply impressive job titles. It means speakers are confirmed, briefed and prepared well ahead of time — and that when inevitable last-minute changes happen, you're able to find solutions quickly. It also means developing relationships that extend beyond a single event, turning speakers and contributors into long-term members of the MedTech World ecosystem. Ultimately, you'll help shape the voice of MedTech World across four global regions and build the conversations connecting our international community. Why Join MedTech World? Malta-based or remote Our headquarters are in Malta, and we'd love to have you working alongside our team here. However, if you're not based in Malta, this role can also be performed remotely, with regular collaboration across our international team and travel to key MedTech World events. Relocation support If you'd like to relocate to Malta, we'll help make the transition easier, including shared temporary accommodation for your first two months. Build something global You'll help shape conferences across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Asia, with flagship gatherings in Malta, Dubai, West Palm Beach and Hong Kong. Direct access & responsibility You'll work closely with our CEO and senior leadership, with real ownership over the conversations, speakers and ideas that appear on MedTech World stages. International exposure You'll regularly interact with founders, investors, healthcare executives, multinational companies, clinicians and policymakers from around the world. Travel the world Your role may take you to MedTech World summits, roadshows, investor gatherings and other international events throughout the year. Growth & ownership MedTech World is still growing rapidly. You'll have the opportunity to build new formats, shape our global content strategy, take ownership and grow your responsibilities alongside the organisation. Work & Wander Eligible team members may extend selected business trips across our international hubs, combining remote working with time to explore the destination. T&Cs apply. Flexible hours Start your working day anytime between 07:30 and 09:00, with flexibility when working across international markets and time zones. Ready to Shape the Conversations Driving the Future of Healthcare? If you're driven by impact, excited by international travel, and ready to take on your events career to another level - we’d love to meet you. Apply now and help bring the MedTech World vision to life.
